scope: Magnitude of a source-specific contaminant change, separate from direction, certainty, significance, safety and net benefit.
rationale: The owner requested Low, Moderate and High magnitude labels using editorial judgment. Quarter- and half-baseline boundaries provide a simple, reproducible display convention; these are not validated scientific efficacy cutoffs or occurrence-reference quartiles.

reported_assessments.locator: Abstract; Methods: Cooking rice in different volumes of water; Results paragraphs 2–3 and Figure 1.
reported_assessments.basis: Source-reported central reduction, 57 ± 5%. The unresolved ± definition is not converted to a confidence interval; the magnitude label describes the central estimate only.

reported_assessments.locator: Get strategies for rice and infant rice cereal; paragraphs on pasta-style cooking and nutrient losses.
reported_assessments.basis: FDA research summary gives a 40–60% reduction depending on rice type. The range spans Moderate and High; no midpoint or universal household effect is assigned.

reported_assessments.locator: Final paragraph under Get strategies for rice and infant rice cereal.
reported_assessments.basis: FDA describes a minimal effect on arsenic in cooked grain. Low is an explicitly qualitative editorial interpretation of that wording; no percentage or species-specific iAs reduction is inferred.
